page: Microsoft Azure D248lds_v7 is an x86_64 compute instance belonging to the low-memory Dldsv7 server family. It is built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization and features 248 dedicated Intel processor vCPUs alongside 496.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server incorporates zero GPUs and comes without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Storage configuration includes 15,118 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD capacity, and the architecture supports Azure Premium Storage. The local disk configuration affords direct access to substantial solid-state storage without relying entirely on remote network-attached disks for high-throughput disk operations.

Hardware resource tradeoffs on the D248lds_v7 focus on compute density and direct disk throughput at the expense of memory footprint. With a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, it operates with lower memory per core than standard general-purpose profiles. Cost efficiency is centered on high core counts paired directly with high local NVMe density, reducing unnecessary expenditure on surplus RAM. Workload fit includes high-concurrency batch processing, large-scale compilation, distributed computing, and data pipelines requiring massive local scratch storage.
